The queue page can't be reached by clicking, and it highlights the wrong tab: the AI tab bar (Inbox … Tests) has no Queue tab, and INBOX is lit while the page shows "Task queue" (page 5, navigation 4). Evidence: shots/…-ai-queue/1200.png, top band; shots/…-ai/1200.png has no link to the queue.

At 1920 the table columns squeeze the task title to about 190 px. Every title wraps to 3–4 lines, only 6 rows fit on screen, and wide gaps sit between Re-asked, State and Score (layout 3). Evidence: shots/…-ai-queue/1920.png, list band. The 1700 px breakpoint is a viewport query, but the list sits beside a sidebar, the summary column and the dictation panel.

At 1700 px and wider, `.tq-label { display: none }` also hides the "Importance", "Cost" and "Re-asks" labels in the "How it is ranked" box, so its three rules read as unlabeled fragments ("the big thing it serves: #1 = 3…") (words 11). Evidence: shots/…-ai-queue/1920.png and 3440.png, left box, against 1200.png, where the labels show. Scope the hide to `.tq-row .tq-label`.

The priority doesn't separate anything yet: all 20 rows score 0.74, cost $6.05, big thing #1 and 0× re-asks (requirements: "prioritizes … based on cost … importance"). Evidence: shots/…-ai-queue/3440.png, rows 1–9. plan.md already names this weakness and its next step (a tie-break by oldest ask, a per-template estimate).

The "Why" cell says "the owner's ask" on every row. The record has a `why` (`priority.why`, set in `TaskQueue.row`), but the page doesn't show it, so the reason itself never appears (page 9). Evidence: shots/…-ai-queue/3440.png, Why column.

At 1200 each card stacks Cost, Big thing, Re-asked and state on four separate lines, so only 4 tasks fit on the first screen (layout 10, page 10). Evidence: shots/…-ai-queue/1200.png. One meta line per card would fit at least twice as many.

Padding stacks up. At 400 the first paragraph sits 55 px from the edge (tq-side 15 + tq-view 12 + page 28), over the 3em limit, and the page's gaps are em constants plus a private `clamp(0.6em, 3cqi, 1.5em)` instead of `--pad`/`--gap` (spacing 33, 34, 37). Evidence: layout.json left_stack.p at 400.
The task went over budget: it spent $11.03 against the brief's $8 (session.jsonl, the 20:20 heartbeat line).
Muted text uses `opacity` (`.tq-label`, `.tq-crumb`, `.tq-note`, `.tq-h`) instead of the `.muted` class (colour 8). Each width also logs a 404 for a missing resource (layout.json errors).

The queue uses about a third of the screen on desktop. At 1200 the list column is about 245 px wide, so every title wraps to 4 or 5 lines, and an empty gutter of about 300 px sits left of the summary card. At 3440 the whole view is about 880 px wide in a 2800 px main (layout 1, 3, 9) — shots/…-queue/1200.png and 3440.png, middle band; layout.json tq-view share 3.85 / ink 0.23 at 1200. `--measure: none` on `.tq-page` does not reach whatever caps the width.

At 400 the padding stacks to 55 px at the paragraph's left edge, over three padded layers: tq-side 15 + tq-view 12 + page 28 (spacing 33, 34) — layout.json left_stack.p at 400. The summary card's border and padding sit inside the view's padding, which sits inside the page's padding.

The list switches to table columns only at 3440. At 1920 it is still cards, yet plan.md says "At 1920 … the list becomes table columns" and the readme says "table columns above 1700 px". The container query `min-width: 60em` on `.tq-main` is what decides (finding 1 keeps the container narrow) — shots/…-queue/1920.png.

The look does not yet show a ranking. Rows 1–7+ all score 0.74 with the same $6.05 estimate, big thing #1 and 0 re-asks, so the order is just "oldest first" (requirements 2, priority). plan.md names this weakness and the tie-break as the next step — 3440.png, list.
At 400 the summary and formula card fills the first screen, and the queue itself starts below the fold (flow 25) — 400.png, band 2. The list is what the owner opens the page for.
The AI tab bar has no Queue tab, and INBOX shows as active while the queue page is open (navigation 3/4). The page is in `children:`, but the reader cannot see where they are — every shot, top band.
Every "why" link reads "the owner's ask", so ten identical orange links say nothing about which ask (page 8, 9) — 1920.png, list.
Muted text is made with `opacity` 0.55–0.7, not `.muted`. The 0.78em breadcrumb at 0.65 is likely under 4.5:1 (colour 1, 8). Gaps and padding are em constants, not the spacing clamp (spacing 37).
layout.json shows one 404 resource at every width, on this page and on /framework/ai/.

The priority does not rank anything yet: rows 1–10 all show $6.05, big thing #1, re-asked 0× and score 0.74 (requirement 2, "priority"). The cost is one median per module, so every `ai` task costs the same, and re-asks are 0 everywhere. In practice the order is "big thing, then oldest", not the owner's "cost, importance, re-asks". shots/…-queue/1200.png, the list band; plan.md admits the tie.

The page has no side padding. "Task queue" and the list start at x≈0 at 400 and about 2px from the sidebar edge at 1200 and 3440, so the title and the cards touch the edge of the screen (spacing 1). See shots/…-queue/400.png, top and second bands, and 1200.png, the title band.

At 3440 the table stretches across about 1400px. The Why column sits about 300px right of the titles, Cost is far right of that, and the gap between them is empty (layout 2, wasted space). See shots/…-queue/3440.png, the list band, and layout.json `empty 0.456`.
At 400 the summary and the formula ("How it is ranked") sit below all 20 cards, so a phone never sees why the rows are in this order (flow 1). See shots/…-queue/400.png.

`ai/queue/files.jsonl` lists two sed temp files (`sedWxAbd7`, `sedNaddHh`) and then marks them gone. `page.jsonl` (weight 3) and `settings.jsonl` (weight 1) also give the same page two different weights. Both come from the diff.
`TaskQueueView.change()` only ever sets rows, so a task that lands is never removed from the live list until the page reloads (requirement 2, "live"). From the diff, TaskQueueView.js, `change(r)`.
At 3440 the "RE-ASKED" column header wraps to two lines (wrapping 1). See shots/…-queue/3440.png, the column-heading row.

The priority column doesn't rank anything you can see: the top 10 rows (at least) all score 0.74, all cost $6.05, are all "Big thing #1" and all re-asked 0×. That fails the owner's "prioritizes things based on cost … priority … if I keep asking" (Requirements 3). Evidence: shots/…-queue/3440.png, rows 1–10. plan.md names this weakness, but the look is the thing being approved. Before the shot is shown, the estimate needs to vary per task (by template or by title), or the tie-break needs to show (oldest first).

On a phone the summary column ("143 tasks queued", the three big things, the formula) is moved below all 20 cards (`.tq-side { order: 2 }`). The reader sees 20 identical 0.74 cards before learning what the page is (page structure). Evidence: shots/…-queue/400.png, where nothing above the list says what is ranked or how.

At 3440 the table columns spread out: each title ends near x≈830 and its Why starts at x≈1090. Cost, Big, Re-asks and State float far to the right of the Why. The row is hard to read across (layout/sizing). Evidence: shots/…-queue/3440.png, list band; layout.json widest_text 705.
"Big thing #1" repeats the "serves priority 1: See and approve the work" text in the same row, so each card says it twice (words). Evidence: shots/…-queue/1200.png, every row.
`ai/queue/files.jsonl` records two sed temp files (`sedWxAbd7`, `sedNaddHh`) and then marks them gone. These are junk lines in the folder's file index (diff, files.jsonl lines 6–9).
Every width logs a 404 (layout.json errors, both pages). The missing resource isn't named; check whether it is the queue page's.

Law 6: `TaskQueue` is a second ranking beside `Task.rank`. what-exists.md gives the reason (neither ranks by cost or re-asks), and the reason is sound. TaskLoop doesn't read it yet, so for now there are two orders.
